_comment_template: #{{UNCATEGORIZED}} is present so uncategorised entries render HERE rather than being appended after everything else. It is placement, not safety: this action appends them under defaultCategory by default, so nothing is lost either way. The upstream mikepenz action DROPS them without the placeholder -- that difference is why this is spelled out.
_comment_default: defaultCategory MUST NOT be set to an empty string. That is the one setting that silently discards an entry matching no category, which for a release note is the worst available outcome.
_comment_commit_template: Subject line only. Commit bodies in this repo run to dozens of lines each, so including one would turn every release note into a transcript.
_comment_ignore: Merge commits carry no information a reader wants in a release note, and this history has them. ignore_rules DROPS a matching entry entirely -- the one place dropping is correct, because a merge is not a change.
_comment_categories: Keyed on Conventional Commits prefixes. This repo's history does NOT use them yet, so entries currently land under Other Changes -- which is correct behaviour, not a failure, and is why defaultCategory above is load-bearing today rather than a fallback.
